### Problem: Longest common subsequence {#sec-st-p1-lcs}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the length of the longest common subsequence of `text1` and `text2`.

$1 \le n, m \le 1000$. On `abcde` and `ace` the answer is 3. On `abc` and `abc` the answer is 3. On `abc` and `def` the answer is 0.

Source: [LC 1143 · Longest Common Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-subsequence/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
If the last letters are equal, some longest common subsequence matches them to each other: the rest is the answer on the two shorter prefixes. If they differ, at least one of them is unused, so the answer is the better of the two ways to drop one letter. Matching `z` first in `zab` against `abz` scores 1. Skipping both `z`s scores 2.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $L[i][j]$ = LCS length of $s[0..i)$ and $t[0..j)$.
- **Transition.** Equal last letters: $L[i - 1][j - 1] + 1$. Otherwise $\max(L[i - 1][j],\ L[i][j - 1])$.
- **Base.** $L[i][0] = L[0][j] = 0$. **Answer.** $L[n][m]$. **Order.** Increasing $i$, and increasing $j$ inside the row.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` is the LCS of the prefixes of lengths `i` and `j`. Empty prefix answers 0. Equal last letters make one call on `(i - 1, j - 1)`. Different last letters take the better of the two drops.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lcs", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-lcs-rec
def lcs_rec(a, b):
    def f(i, j):
        if i == 0 or j == 0:
            return 0
        if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
            return f(i - 1, j - 1) + 1
        return max(f(i - 1, j), f(i, j - 1))
    return f(len(a), len(b))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lcsRec(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b) {
    if (i == 0 || j == 0) return 0;
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return lcsRec(i - 1, j - 1, a, b) + 1;
    return max(lcsRec(i - 1, j, a, b), lcsRec(i, j - 1, a, b));
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
There are `(n + 1)(m + 1)` pairs. Store each one. The body is the previous button.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lcs", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-lcs-memo
def lcs_memo(a, b):
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    memo = [[None] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]

    def f(i, j):
        if memo[i][j] is None:
            if i == 0 or j == 0:
                memo[i][j] = 0
            elif a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                memo[i][j] = f(i - 1, j - 1) + 1
            else:
                memo[i][j] = max(f(i - 1, j), f(i, j - 1))
        return memo[i][j]

    return f(n, m)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lcsMemo(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (i == 0 || j == 0) return memo[i][j] = 0;
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return memo[i][j] = lcsMemo(i - 1, j - 1, a, b, memo) + 1;
    return memo[i][j] = max(lcsMemo(i - 1, j, a, b, memo), lcsMemo(i, j - 1, a, b, memo));
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Fill the grid from the top-left. The calls go away. Walking back from the corner, a diagonal step on equal letters appends that letter; otherwise step toward the neighbour that holds the same length. The collected letters are one LCS, in reverse.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lcs", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-lcs-tab
def lcs_tab(a, b):
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1
            else:
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    seq, i, j = [], n, m
    while i and j:
        if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] and dp[i][j] == dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1:
            seq.append(a[i - 1])
            i, j = i - 1, j - 1
        elif dp[i - 1][j] >= dp[i][j - 1]:
            i -= 1
        else:
            j -= 1
    seq.reverse()
    return dp[n][m], "".join(seq)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lcsTab(const string& a, const string& b, string& seq) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<vector<int>> dp(n + 1, vector<int>(m + 1));
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
            dp[i][j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 : max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
    int i = n, j = m;
    while (i && j) {
        if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] && dp[i][j] == dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1) {
            seq.push_back(a[i - 1]);
            --i; --j;
        } else if (dp[i - 1][j] >= dp[i][j - 1]) --i;
        else --j;
    }
    reverse(seq.begin(), seq.end());
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### One row

::: {.form-next}
Only the previous row is needed for the length. `prev[j]` is the row above, `cur[j - 1]` is the cell to the left, and `prev[j - 1]` is the diagonal. The string is not recovered from this row. Call the table when you need the letters.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lcs", "row")
    assert str(final) == "3"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-lcs-row
def lcs_row(a, b):
    if len(a) < len(b):
        a, b = b, a
    prev = [0] * (len(b) + 1)
    for ca in a:
        cur = [0]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            if ca == cb:
                cur.append(prev[j - 1] + 1)
            else:
                cur.append(max(prev[j], cur[j - 1]))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]

assert lcs_rec("abcde", "ace") == lcs_memo("abcde", "ace") == 3
assert lcs_tab("abcde", "ace") == (3, "ace")
assert lcs_row("abcde", "ace") == 3
assert lcs_row("abc", "abc") == 3 and lcs_row("abc", "def") == 0
assert lcs_tab("zab", "abz")[0] == 2
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lcsRow(string a, string b) {
    if (a.size() < b.size()) swap(a, b);
    vector<int> prev(b.size() + 1), cur(b.size() + 1);
    for (char ca : a) {
        cur[0] = 0;
        for (int j = 1; j <= (int)b.size(); ++j)
            cur[j] = ca == b[j - 1] ? prev[j - 1] + 1 : max(prev[j], cur[j - 1]);
        swap(prev, cur);
    }
    return prev.back();
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** follows every way to drop letters. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$ time and memory. **One row** is $O(nm)$ time and $O(\min(n, m))$ memory. $n, m \le 1000$ allows the table, which is what reconstruction needs.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- No letter in common: the corner stays 0, and the walk prints nothing.
- One string is a subsequence of the other: the answer is the shorter length.
- Two equal strings: the answer is the length, and the walk prints the string.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Returning a cell other than the corner. Every prefix pair has its own LCS. The strings in the statement are the full prefixes.
- A greedy earliest match. `zab` against `abz` scores 1 that way and 2 if both `z`s are skipped.
- Reading the diagonal after the cell above has already overwritten it, in a one-array roll that is not saved. Keep the previous row, or save `prev[j - 1]` before you write.
:::

**Variants.** A common subarray cannot skip, so a mismatch resets the length to 0 instead of taking a max of the drops: [LC 718 · Maximum Length of Repeated Subarray](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-length-of-repeated-subarray/){difficulty="Medium"}. The dot product of two subsequences puts the product on the diagonal and still allows either drop: [LC 1458 · Max Dot Product of Two Subsequences](https://leetcode.com/problems/max-dot-product-of-two-subsequences/){difficulty="Hard"}. Deleting until the two strings are equal, with no replacements, is $n + m - 2 \cdot \mathrm{LCS}$: [LC 583 · Delete Operation for Two Strings](https://leetcode.com/problems/delete-operation-for-two-strings/){difficulty="Medium"}.
